transcription.name: Jyutping
transcription.note: The wikitext attempt reads the |c= parameter of the {{zh-pron}} template, which Wiktionary keeps as the canonical Cantonese reading; a comma starts an alternative reading and is not taken. A simplified-form or variant-form page only points at its main form through {{zh-see}}, so the wikitext attempt follows that pointer and the later attempts ask for the form it named.

transcription.name: Yale
transcription.note: Cantonese Yale. Wiktionary derives it from the Jyutping at render time, so only the rendered page carries it. The Mandarin box prints a Yale line too, so the match anchors on the link to the Cantonese Yale article. The span strategy is required because a tone mark with an alternative is wrapped in a help span, which a flat pattern would truncate. The article page is asked before the REST rendering, because the REST host rejects bursts with 429.

note: Language pack for Cantonese. Every URL and extraction rule is data — edit here, no recompile. The 'pronunciation' and 'audio' lists are independent and each is shown in the order written here. Cantonese transcriptions are read as IPA, not as Jyutping, so the sources listed are the ones that publish IPA. Every source is read from an ordinary article page rather than a machine API, because the article hosts impose no request ceiling while the REST endpoints reject bursts with 429, which the reader would report as an unreachable source.

pronunciation.name: Wiktionary
pronunciation.note: The Chinese pronunciation table of an entry carries one row per variety. Only the Cantonese row links its IPA key to the Cantonese phonology article, so that link anchors the reader to the right row and keeps Mandarin, Hakka and Min readings out. The span strategy is required because the transcription nests tone-note spans inside the IPA span, which a flat pattern would truncate. An entry with no Cantonese section carries no anchor, so the attempt simply yields nothing.

pronunciation.name: Chinese Wiktionary
pronunciation.note: The Chinese Wiktionary prints the same transcription behind a Chinese anchor, where the key of the Cantonese row links to the 粵語音系 article and the label reads 幫助. Its coverage of colloquial Cantonese headwords is thinner than the English one, so it stands second.

audio.name: Wiktionary
audio.note: Wiktionary embeds Commons recordings as protocol-relative addresses, so 'prefix' supplies the scheme. Only the transcoded mp3 rendition is taken, because the original is WAV or Opus. The first attempt takes a Lingua Libre LL-Q9186_%28yue%29- filename and the second a Zh-yue- one, and both prefixes mark the recording as Cantonese rather than Mandarin.
